verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Equivalent, with the four formulas of this one display distributed over one theorem and several definitions, and with one convention. Term by term: W_ab = ⟨w_a w_b⟩_θ is `State.covariance` (the angular average of `bilinearCovariance`); P = ∫⟨g_r⟩_Y dR is `pressureDefect = radialMoment 0 (u.gr c)`, which unfolds to `PressureStream.pressureMass (g_r)` = ∫ r, torusAverage g_r — the same radial integral of the torus average that occurs inside the Lean's pressure; p_m = T_0(g_r − ρP) is `VariableGaugeMean.meanPressure`, whose source is literally `f z - density … * pressureMass f z.2.1` and whose T_0 is `compactPrimitive` (the Lean's ρ is the gauge-rescaled `VariableGaugeMean.density`, of integral one like the paper's ρ); and the mean equation itself is `angularMean_fullResidual`, whose right-hand side `meanResidual` is `reducedMeanResidual + meanBaseError`, with the three components of `reducedMeanResidual` being `radialResidual = D_r p_m − g_r`, `thetaResidual = E_θ` and `axialResidual = E_z`. So the paper's ⟨G_* + F_* − E_{B,*}⟩_θ corresponds to ⟨fullResidual⟩_θ minus the stored base error, the paper subtracting on the left what the Lean adds on the right. The convention: the Lean states the identity in normalized chart variables, so the starred rescaling by Q^{2A+1/2} that the paper applies to G, F and E_B before taking the angular mean is absorbed into the chart and does not appear; the rescaling is a single common positive factor on both sides of an identity, so it may be divided out.
